16	+## Why this matters
17	+ILM/DLM are TCM (tightly-coupled memory) = single-cycle local RAM, the most
18	+performance-relevant memory in the AE350. Today the content is NOT transported
19	+(3 gaps: not in the shared mmap, plugin does not drain it, vsim `load_elf` only

25	+feeds them to the vsim leg via the EXISTING `--ilm`/`--dlm` args; vsim's existing

+# ROADMAP: ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff (Approach A)
+
+Goal: make Hart 0 ILM (`0xA0000000..0xA01FFFFF`) and DLM (`0xA0200000..0xA03FFFFF`)
+memory CONTENT survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff, so a benchmark whose hot
+code/data lives in TCM measures correct results and correct cycles.
+
+Scope: content only. The config CSRs (`milmb`/`mdlmb`) are already transported in
+the v3 Andes block (verify-excluded). This roadmap is about the bytes.
+
+## Why this matters
+ILM/DLM are TCM (tightly-coupled memory) = single-cycle local RAM, the most
+performance-relevant memory in the AE350. Today the content is NOT transported
+(3 gaps: not in the shared mmap, plugin does not drain it, vsim `load_elf` only
+targets main_memory). vsim resumes with ILM/DLM at RTL reset (empty). Latent
+today (no fixture uses TCM); breaks/mis-measures any TCM benchmark.
+
+## Chosen approach: A (file sidecar + reuse `--ilm`/`--dlm`)
+Plugin drains ILM/DLM to sidecar files next to the state `--outfile`; the driver
+feeds them to the vsim leg via the EXISTING `--ilm`/`--dlm` args; vsim's existing
+`load_image` backdoor writes them into the RTL.
+
+Key reason A wins: the vsim restore leg already exists and is nearly free.
+- `--ilm`/`--dlm` -> `Simulator::load_image` (`vsim: src/simulator.hpp:524`)
+  -> `cpu.set_ilm`/`set_dlm`
+  (`vsim: src/cpu_wrappers/ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp:392,466`).
+- `set_ilm` is NOT a bus/PB/DMI transfer. It is a Verilator hierarchical-reference
+  poke straight into the model SRAM array (`rootp->..__DOT__..mem[i] = word`),
+  costs zero sim cycles, and regenerates ECC/parity itself. So the plugin only
+  needs to drain RAW data; vsim rebuilds ECC.
+- No ABI change: content rides sidecar files, `hybrid_state_v1` is untouched.
+
+Alternatives (not chosen now): B shared-mmap-backed ILM/DLM (less invasive per
+run but changes mmap layout on both sides + QEMU device model); C add an ABI
+block (96KB into the state file, larger ABI surface). Revisit only if A hits a
+wall.
+
+## Established facts (verified in code; trust these, do not re-derive)
+- QEMU slave port: `subport_create` (`qemu: hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1381`) maps
+  `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000` as `memory_region_init_io` with `subport_ops`, which
+  dispatch to the hart-local `env->mask_ilm`/`env->mask_dlm`
+  (`qemu: target/riscv/cpu_helper.c:1308-1330`). So the slave port aliases the
+  real ILM/DLM content.
+- TCM overlay is PER-CPU, not system memory: `andes_cpu_lm_realize`
+  (`qemu: target/riscv/cpu.c:673-696`) does `memory_region_init_ram` then
+  `memory_region_add_subregion_overlap(env->cpu_as_root, ...)` - the overlay
+  exists only in the CPU's address space, and only when `*_default_enable` is on
+  (dynamic enable via a guest `milmb` write is handled around
+  `qemu: target/riscv/andes_csr.c:1270`; F0 confirms that path in practice).
+- CONSEQUENCE - runtime-populate is REQUIRED, static-init is dead on arrival:
+  QEMU's ELF loader writes SYSTEM memory (DRAM). A static-initialized section
+  with a TCM VMA lands in DRAM; a hart with the overlay enabled then reads the
+  TCM (zeros) at that address, never the loaded bytes. So for BOTH ILM and DLM
+  the fixture itself must write the content at runtime (which is also how real
+  silicon TCM is populated - crt0/program copies it in). This kills any
+  "linker-places-static-sections-into-TCM" fixture design.
+- Sizes are configurable, NOT fixed. QEMU builds the actual RAM at the property
+  size: `qemu.cfg ilm_size` -> SoC prop -> `env->ilm_size`
+  (`qemu: target/riscv/cpu.c:640,643`) -> `memory_region_init_ram(env->mask_ilm,
+  env->ilm_size)` (`cpu.c:673`). `ax45mpv_premium` = ILM 64KB / DLM 32KB via the
+  `--print-qemu-config` -> `-readconfig qemu.cfg` path (`ilm_size=65536`,
+  `dlm_size=32768`, `*_default_enable=on`). QEMU compiled-in defaults are 2MB/2MB
+  + enable=off (the raw path plugin tests use). Only the slave-port ADDRESS
+  window is fixed (2MB in the memmap); just the first `ilm_size` bytes are
+  RAM-backed. Valid size 0 or pow2 in [1KB, 512MB].
+- Hart-local TCM ranges on the premium engine: ILM `0x0..0xFFFF` (64KB),

+/* LM content transport e2e (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm F4a): DLM data round-trip.
+ *
+ *   QEMU 1: enable the DLM (csr 0x7C1 mdlmb.EN=1 -- the premium RTL resets
+ *           EN=0, and this CSR write is what arms the write-mask restore on
+ *           the vsim leg), then fill the whole 32 KB window with a
+ *           runtime-COMPUTED pattern through the hart-local view (0x200000).
+ *   vsim:   inside the ROI, re-derive the formula and compare every word of
+ *           the DLM, then print the verdict (DLM_OK / DLM_BAD). The harness
+ *           greps the vsim log (CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK); code after the
+ *           exit marker never runs on the vsim leg, so the verdict must be
+ *           printed INSIDE the ROI (this fixture measures correctness, not
+ *           cycles -- the UART cost is irrelevant).
+ *
+ * Why this is decisive for the transport: the pattern bytes exist NOWHERE
+ * except the local memory. They are runtime-computed (not in the ELF), and
+ * the QEMU-phase stores land in the per-CPU DLM overlay -- NOT the shared
+ * DRAM mmap (QEMU maps the TCM in cpu_as_root; the ELF loader and the mmap
+ * only cover system DRAM). The ONLY road they can travel to the vsim RTL's
+ * DLM SRAM is the sidecar transport: plugin slave-port drain ->
+ * <state>.dlm -> --dlm backdoor load. No transport => vsim reads
+ * reset-empty SRAM => DLM_BAD.
+ *
+ * Geometry: premium hart-0 DLM = 32 KB at hart-local 0x200000 (the program
+ * image ends ~0x10a000 and the stack sits at 0x700000, so nothing else
+ * touches the window). ILM code transport is F4b's job.
+ */
+#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
+
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+
+#define DLM_BASE  0x200000u
+#define DLM_BYTES 32768u
+#define DLM_WORDS (DLM_BYTES / 4u)
+
+/* Per-word pattern: cheap, position-dependent, never all-zero. */
+static inline uint32_t pat(uint32_t i) { return i * 2654435761u + 0x5A17u; }
+
+int main(void)
+{
+  volatile uint32_t *dlm = (volatile uint32_t *) (uintptr_t) DLM_BASE;
+  uint64_t v;
+
+  /* Enable the DLM like real TCM firmware (read-modify-write keeps the
+   * WARL base/size fields). */
+  __asm__ volatile("csrr %0, 0x7c1" : "=r"(v));
+  __asm__ volatile("csrw 0x7c1, %0" ::"r"(v | 1));
+  __asm__ volatile("fence" ::: "memory");
+
+  /* QEMU phase: runtime-computed fill. Also init stdio here so the ROI's
+   * verdict printf does not pay first-call setup inside the window. */
+  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < DLM_WORDS; i++) dlm[i] = pat(i);
+  printf("DLM filled\n");
+  fflush(stdout);
+
+  enter_vsim();
+
+  /* vsim ROI: every word must have crossed the handoff intact. */
+  uint32_t bad = 0, first = 0;
+  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < DLM_WORDS; i++) {
+    if (dlm[i] != pat(i)) {
+      if (bad == 0) first = i;
+      bad++;
+    }
+  }
+  if (bad == 0) {
+    printf("DLM_OK words=%u\n", (unsigned) DLM_WORDS);
+  } else {
+    printf("DLM_BAD count=%u first=%u got=0x%08x want=0x%08x\n",
+           (unsigned) bad, (unsigned) first, (unsigned) dlm[first],
+           (unsigned) pat(first));
+  }
+  fflush(stdout);
+
+  exit_vsim();
+
+  return bad != 0;
+}

+/* LM content transport e2e (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm F4b): ILM CODE round-trip.
+ *
+ *   QEMU 1: enable the ILM (csr 0x7C0 milmb.EN=1 -- arms the write-mask
+ *           restore), assemble a 3-insn kernel a0 = (a0 ^ IMM) + 0x321 into
+ *           hart-local ILM at 0x100 (word stores + fence.i), and call it once
+ *           as a pre-handoff sanity check. IMM comes from a volatile at
+ *           runtime and is PATCHED into the xori encoding, so the correct
+ *           answer depends on the exact instruction bytes transported -- a
+ *           stale or garbled ILM cannot pass.
+ *   vsim:   inside the ROI, call the function pointer at 0x100 -- the fetch
+ *           comes from the ILM RTL SRAM (backdoor-loaded from the sidecar) --
+ *           and print the verdict (ILM_OK / ILM_BAD). Harness greps the vsim
+ *           log (CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK).
+ *
+ * Failure is loud: an empty ILM fetches all-zero words, and 0x00000000 is a
+ * defined illegal instruction on RISC-V -- the trap-free ROI crashes, on top
+ * of the missing verdict.
+ *
+ * Geometry: the harness passes the engine's ILM/DLM sizes to QEMU (-global),
+ * so the overlay is 64 KB at 0x0..0xFFFF -- below the program image at
+ * 0x100000. (QEMU's compiled-in 2 MB default would shadow the program the
+ * moment EN goes high; that is a harness-geometry bug this fixture exists to
+ * catch.) The kernel sits at 0x100, clear of the C NULL address.
+ */
+#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
+
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+
+#define ILM_FN_ADDR 0x100u
+
+typedef uint32_t (*ilm_fn)(uint32_t);
+
+/* Runtime-volatile so the compiler cannot fold the expected value NOR the
+ * patched instruction into constants -- both derive from a memory read. */
+static volatile uint32_t imm_src = 0x5A5u;
+
+int main(void)
+{
+  uint64_t v;
+
+  /* Enable the ILM like real TCM firmware (RMW keeps WARL base/size). */
+  __asm__ volatile("csrr %0, 0x7c0" : "=r"(v));
+  __asm__ volatile("csrw 0x7c0, %0" ::"r"(v | 1));
+  __asm__ volatile("fence" ::: "memory");
+
+  /* Assemble the kernel into ILM:
+   *   xori a0, a0, IMM   -- IMM patched at runtime (I-type, base 0x00054513)
+   *   addi a0, a0, 0x321 -- 0x32150513
+   *   ret                -- 0x00008067                                    */
+  const uint32_t imm = imm_src & 0xFFFu;
+  volatile uint32_t *ilm = (volatile uint32_t *) (uintptr_t) ILM_FN_ADDR;
+  ilm[0] = 0x00054513u | (imm << 20);
+  ilm[1] = 0x32150513u;
+  ilm[2] = 0x00008067u;
+  __asm__ volatile("fence.i" ::: "memory");
+
+  ilm_fn f = (ilm_fn) (uintptr_t) ILM_FN_ADDR;
+  const uint32_t x = 0x1234u;
+  const uint32_t want = (x ^ imm) + 0x321u;
+
+  /* Pre-handoff sanity: QEMU must execute from its ILM overlay. A failure
+   * here is a fast-leg problem, not a transport problem. */
+  if (f(x) != want) {
+    printf("ILM_QEMU_BAD\n");
+    fflush(stdout);
+    return 2;
+  }
+  printf("ILM staged\n");
+  fflush(stdout);
+
+  enter_vsim();
+
+  /* vsim ROI: the fetch at 0x100 hits the ILM RTL. */
+  uint32_t got = f(x);
+  if (got == want) {
+    printf("ILM_OK got=0x%08x\n", (unsigned) got);
+  } else {
+    printf("ILM_BAD got=0x%08x want=0x%08x\n", (unsigned) got,
+           (unsigned) want);
+  }
+  fflush(stdout);
+
+  exit_vsim();
+
+  return got != want;
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# LM transport (F0/F1) contract: the QEMU plugin drains ILM/DLM CONTENT into
+# raw sidecar files next to the state outfile. The lm_drain fixture writes
+# known patterns into the hart-0 LM slave ports (ILM 0xA0000000, DLM
+# 0xA0200000) at the first and last word of each drained span; the plugin,
+# given ilm_size=/dlm_size=, must write <outfile>.ilm (65536 B) and
+# <outfile>.dlm (32768 B) carrying those patterns. A run WITHOUT the size
+# args (the no-LM-engine default) must produce NO sidecar files.
+#
+# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
+#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
+#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
+#   VSIM_ELF     the lm_drain fixture (FIXTURE=lm_drain)
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
+
+FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_drain}"
+hybrid_resolve_paths
+
+SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
+SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-lm-shared.XXXXXX)
+STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
+STATE_QEMU="$STATE_DIR/state.bin"
+QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
+trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$QEMU_LOG"; rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"' EXIT
+truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
+
+run_qemu() {  # $1 = extra plugin args appended after outfile ("" for none)
+  set +e
+  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
+    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
+    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
+    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
+    -nographic \
+    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
+    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
+    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU$1" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
+  RC=$?
+  set -e
+}
+
+check_word() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 expected LE word (8 hex digits)
+  local got
+  got=$(od -An -tx4 -j "$2" -N4 "$1" | tr -d ' \n')
+  if [ "$got" != "$3" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: $1 @ offset $2 = '$got', want '$3'"
+    exit 1
+  fi

+

+run_qemu ",ilm_size=65536,dlm_size=32768"

+  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
+  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
+  exit 1
+fi
+for spec in "$STATE_QEMU.ilm:65536" "$STATE_QEMU.dlm:32768"; do
+  path="${spec%:*}"; want="${spec#*:}"
+  if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: missing sidecar $path"; exit 1
+  fi
+  size=$(stat -c%s "$path")
+  if [ "$size" -ne "$want" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: $path size=$size want=$want"; exit 1
+  fi
+done

+check_word "$STATE_QEMU.ilm" 65532 494c4d31   # "ILM1" at last drained word
+check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 0     444c4d30   # "DLM0" at window start
+check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 32764 444c4d31   # "DLM1" at last drained word
+

+  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: (no-size run) expected exit=200, got $RC"
+  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
+  exit 1
+fi

+  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: sidecar files written without ilm_size/dlm_size"

+# pattern offsets mirror lm_readback.c's probes: ILM head 0x10 / tail 0xFFFC,
+# DLM head 0x0 / tail 0x7FFC (bin offsets are window-relative).

+#   VSIM_BIN   sim_ax45mpv_premium

+

+

+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+put_word_le() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 32-bit value
+  local v=$3 bytes="" i
+  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
+    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
+  done
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
+  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
+}

+put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0x10))   $((0x494C4D30))   # ILM head
+put_word_le "$WORK/ilm.bin" $((0xFFFC)) $((0x494C4D31))   # ILM tail
+truncate -s 32768 "$WORK/dlm.bin"
+put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" 0           $((0x444C4D30))   # DLM head
+put_word_le "$WORK/dlm.bin" $((0x7FFC)) $((0x444C4D31))   # DLM tail
+

+timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" --ilm "$WORK/ilm.bin" --dlm "$WORK/dlm.bin" \
+  "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run1.log" 2>&1

+fi

+# --- Run 2: negative control, empty TCM -> the same probe must FAIL ---
+timeout 600 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" >"$WORK/run2.log" 2>&1
+RC=$?

+  echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: probe passed with NO --ilm/--dlm (reads are not hitting TCM)"
+  tail -15 "$WORK/run2.log"
+  exit 1
+fi
+

+# must be non-zero only when the wrapper implements the set_ilm/set_dlm
+# backdoor. Premium has it (real sizes); ax46mpv_advanced's config has the
+# memories but its wrapper lacks the backdoor -> must report 0, or the driver
+# would pass --ilm/--dlm and load_image would throw (the F3 ax46 regression).

+  D46=$("$AX46" --describe 2>/dev/null || true)

+    echo "FAIL[vsim_lm_load]: ax46 (no set_ilm/set_dlm backdoor) must describe ilm/dlm 0"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+fi
+

161	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,

180	    77) status=SKIP ;;
181	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
182	  esac
183	  (
184	    flock 9
185	    case "$status" in
186	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
187	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;

202	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
203	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"

212	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
213	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
214	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
215	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
216	done
217	
218	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
219	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
220	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
221	for tm in marker pc; do
222	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
223	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
224	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
225	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
226	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
227	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
228	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
229	  done
230	done

232	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
233	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
234	
235	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
236	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
237	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
238	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
239	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
240	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
241	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
242	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
243	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
244	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
245	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
246	  printf '.\n' >&8
247	done

249	i=0
250	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
251	  i=$((i+1))
252	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
253	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
254	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
255	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
256	  read -r -u 8 _tok
257	  (
258	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
259	    printf '.\n' >&8
260	  ) &
261	done
262	wait
263	exec 8>&-
264	
265	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
266	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
267	  i=$((i+1))
268	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
269	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
270	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
271	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
272	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
273	done

275	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
276	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
277	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

280	  case "$r_status" in
281	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
282	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
283	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
284	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
285	  esac
286	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
287	
288	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
289	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
290	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
291	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
292	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
293	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
294	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
295	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
296	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
297	    echo
298	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
299	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
300	  fi
301	done
302	
303	echo
304	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
305	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
306	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
307	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
308	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
309	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
310	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
311	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
312	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
313	  exit 1
314	fi

  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi
